source_title: Revisiting taxation of capital incomes - Business Standard
source_excerpt: There is a lot of chatter on the need to revisit taxing capital incomes in India, especially incomes from trading in equity. The present regime includes two components — a securities transactions tax (STT) and a capital gains tax. The former is applicable to both purchasing and selling equity while the latter applies to gains from trade in equity, with gains being recognised as long-term if held for more than 12 months. The immediate driver for the conversation stems from a sharp increase in the withdrawal of foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) from equity markets in India. This process has two separate but related consequences — a dramatic drop in returns on investment in equities and a consistent depreciation of the currency. What is the context for this review of policy and how can one think about such a demand for review?
